title: Guard hardening residuals: installer config scope, hermetic tests, README pins, branch disposition

completion_criteria.text: Hook installation reads and writes its hook-path state in ONE config scope, so a global, system, or env-injected core.hooksPath is never recorded as the repository's prior value and never written back as local config. Proven by a test that is RED under hostile ambient config before the fix and green after.

The suite's result does not change when a global core.hooksPath or any GIT_CONFIG_* is present in the environment. Today 4 installer tests fail under that condition while the machine-local run is 622/622.

The ledger's own commit and merge path is unaffected by repository-local content filters and by repository-local signature-verification settings - OR both gaps are recorded as accepted in a decision and named in the README's accepted-gaps list.

The recovery store reports success only when the resulting store is usable, and never adopts a pre-existing unrelated repository at that path. A test covers a store directory that exists but is not a usable repo.
Every line-range citation in the README resolves to the code it claims, verified at the commit where it ships (six ranges are wrong at d102fb8; one lands on a deny while claiming ask).

The two inherited user calls are each recorded as a decision: commit attribution for the Round B `git add -A` sweep, and whether this branch is pushed and opened as one PR through the centralized pr-create tool.
